answer: Reputation momentum with decay resists sybils: standing accrues as a moving average of recent contribution and decays geometrically, so influence reflects sustained recent work, not a one-time spike. An ember of a single good epoch fades unless fed; a swarm cannot bank a pulse of activity and coast, because the moving average pulls each idle fake back toward zero like a river reclaiming its banks. Maintaining a thousand fakes at high momentum demands continuous per-head work every epoch — a relentless, compounding operational cost.
